new_result: A common Fourier envelope min(1,K|t|^-b), b>1, makes the quadratic output density quantitatively stable under product-source L1 perturbations: L-infinity error is O(K^(1/b) Delta^(1-1/b)) and C^{0,alpha} seminorm error is O(K^((alpha+1)/b) Delta^(1-(alpha+1)/b)) for alpha<b-1. At q=4/3 this is <39.233 Z^-1/6 Delta^1/9 and <166.572 Z^-17/96 Delta^1/18 at alpha=1/16. The e5 ruled majority-side interval bound passes to arbitrary rough ambient product inputs by smoothing only the three active original coordinates and using uniform conditional total-variation contraction.
first_unpaid_target: product-provenance-sensitive minority/two-sheet interval or tent bound, plus compatible global structural glue when no uniformly conditioned physical triple exists
